inputs.report:
# Community Solar in the Lakeshire Region

## Introduction
Community solar lets households subscribe to a shared solar project instead of installing panels on their own roofs. This report reviews the current state, benefits, challenges and outlook of community solar in the Lakeshire region.

## Current State
Lakeshire's community solar programs reached 412 MW of installed capacity at the end of 2025, up from 260 MW in 2023 [1]. About 38,000 households now subscribe, most of them renters [1].

## Benefits
Subscribers saved an average of 11% on their annual electricity bills in 2025 [1]. The programs also created 2,400 local construction jobs and cut regional carbon emissions by 27% [1].

## Challenges
The interconnection queue held 96 applications in March 2026, and the median wait from application to connection was 19 months [2]. In a survey of 1,500 residents, 64% said they would join a project if enrollment were simpler [3].

## Outlook
With two substation upgrades planned by 2027 [2], installed capacity is projected to reach 1,150 MW by 2030 and to serve 35% of the region's households [2]. Subscription prices are expected to fall to US$0.06 per kWh [2].

## Conclusion
Community solar has grown quickly in Lakeshire, but interconnection delays and complicated enrollment are slowing further growth.
